newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Wednesday on speculative selling by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,242 yuan ($391) per tonne, losing 57 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,300 yuan per tonne.
The contract is due to deliver on July 22.
September fell three to 3,288 yuan, November two to 3,246, the January 1998 contract 140 to 3,120 and March 80 to 3,120 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 24,400 tonnes from 14,700 tonnes.
Soybeans opened little changed from Tuesday's close but speculative selling pushed prices steadily down before all contracts closed at their lows, traders said.
"Speculative selling is responsible for today's falls and investors are also seen continuing to liquidate their long positions in the July contract," one trader said.
"But soybeans are likely to rebound technically in the next few days after today's losses," he added.
